updates.title: Utah expands supervised AI pilots
updates.summary: Utah’s AI office lists new agreements for Expect Fitness and August AI signed on 2 October 2026, following Nolla Health on 22 September. The pilots cover specified physical-therapy, prescription-refill, and acne-treatment uses.
updates.timing: As checked on 5 October, these three entries are marked approved, with their demonstration periods not yet started.
updates.meaning: A business must obtain its own written agreement with the AI office and relevant regulator. Relief is limited to the named rules, activities, safeguards, and test period; other requirements continue to apply.
updates.context: This is a verified expansion through administrative pilot agreements. It should not be described as a blanket 2025 legislative expansion or permission for any AI company to operate without regulation.

sources.label: Office of AI Policy · signed pilot register

updates.title: Colorado replaces its AI framework; rulemaking underway
updates.summary: SB 26-189, signed on 14 May 2026, repeals and reenacts the earlier SB 24-205 framework. The attorney general filed proposed implementing rules on 11 August 2026, covering automated decisions alongside separate chatbot-safety legislation.
updates.timing: Key ADMT duties start 1 January 2027. The published formal-comment period runs through 26 October 2026, subject to any continuation of the hearing.
updates.meaning: Covered developers and deployers should assess documentation, notices, record retention, correction, and human-review duties against the replacement law and follow the rulemaking before implementation.
updates.context: The description of a Q3 2025 ‘first-year performance’ sunset review is not supported by the sources checked. SB 24-205’s original main duties were scheduled for 2026, and the current framework is the 2026 replacement. Draft rules are not final rules.

updates.title: California’s TFAIA follows its September 2025 signing
updates.summary: Governor Newsom signed SB 53, the Transparency in Frontier Artificial Intelligence Act, on 29 September 2025. Its general effective date is 1 January 2026; individual implementation provisions have their own timing.
updates.timing: California’s Department of Technology must make its first statutory recommendations on updating the frontier-model and developer definitions by 1 January 2027.
updates.meaning: Covered frontier developers should assess incident-reporting and whistleblower protections; large frontier developers also face published safety-framework and transparency duties. Scope depends on statutory model and developer definitions.
updates.context: The September 2025 signing is a historical milestone, not a new October 2026 enactment. CalCompute’s separate provisions depend on an appropriation; the general effective date does not make every programme operational at once.
